# Robots + Sitemap — Last Agency

> Owner: SEO Manager. Implementation: Architect (`app/robots.ts` and `app/sitemap.ts` in Next 14 App Router).
> Domain: `https://lastagency.com`.

---

## 1. `robots.txt` — exact contents

The Architect implements this as `app/robots.ts` returning the equivalent metadata object. The literal generated file should match this byte-for-byte:

```
# Last Agency — robots.txt
# Generated by app/robots.ts at build time.

User-agent: *
Allow: /

# Block API endpoints and Next.js internals
Disallow: /api/
Disallow: /_next/
Disallow: /thanks
Disallow: /404

# Sitemap reference
Sitemap: https://lastagency.com/sitemap.xml

# Host preference (some crawlers honor this)
Host: https://lastagency.com
```

### Why these specific rules

- `Allow: /` is the default; stated explicitly so a future reader doesn't assume we're locked down.
- `Disallow: /api/` keeps the contact form's POST handler out of search results. The Architect's `app/api/contact/route.ts` is server-only; this is belt-and-braces.
- `Disallow: /_next/` keeps build chunks out of search results (Google ignores them anyway; this is for less-smart crawlers).
- `Disallow: /thanks` keeps the post-submit page out — it's a transient state, not a landing page, and ranking it would be confusing.
- `Disallow: /404` keeps the soft 404 URL out (Next renders the not-found page at any unmatched route — we don't want a literal `/404` indexed if someone curls it).
- No `Crawl-delay` — Google ignores it, others rarely matter at our traffic volume.
- No bot-specific allow/deny — we treat all crawlers uniformly until we have a reason not to.

### Next.js `app/robots.ts` equivalent

```ts
import type { MetadataRoute } from 'next';

export default function robots(): MetadataRoute.Robots {
  return {
    rules: [
      {
        userAgent: '*',
        allow: '/',
        disallow: ['/api/', '/_next/', '/thanks', '/404'],
      },
    ],
    sitemap: 'https://lastagency.com/sitemap.xml',
    host: 'https://lastagency.com',
  };
}
```

---

## 2. `sitemap.xml` — strategy

Architect implements as `app/sitemap.ts` returning a `MetadataRoute.Sitemap`. The list of routes is **generated at build time** — case-study routes are read from `content/case-studies.json` (the same file the Testimonial Manager publishes).

### Included routes

| Route | Source | `lastmod` | `changefreq` | `priority` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | static | `BUILD_TIME` (current build's ISO timestamp) | `monthly` | `1.0` |
| `/work` | static | `max(handoffDate)` across all case studies | `monthly` | `0.9` |
| `/services` | static | `BUILD_TIME` | `monthly` | `0.9` |
| `/about` | static | `BUILD_TIME` | `yearly` | `0.7` |
| `/get-in-touch` | static | `BUILD_TIME` | `yearly` | `0.7` |
| `/work/[slug]` | derived from `case-studies.json` | `handoffDate` per entry | `yearly` | `0.8` |

### Excluded routes

- `/get-in-touch/thanks` — transient, post-submit only.
- `/404` (and any unmatched routes hitting `not-found.tsx`) — soft 404, not a landing page.
- Any future `/admin` / `/preview` routes (not in scope for Phase 3 but pre-excluded).

### Why these priorities

- `/` is `1.0` because it's the most-linked, the most-shared, and the page that earns the brand search.
- `/work` and `/services` are `0.9` because they're the two pages a founder actually evaluates us on.
- `/work/[slug]` is `0.8` — high because case studies carry the long-tail intent (brand + outcome searches) but slightly below `/work` so the index page wins ties.
- `/about` and `/get-in-touch` are `0.7` — important for branded queries but rarely the landing target for cold search.

Priority is a hint Google has historically discounted, but it costs nothing to declare and helps smaller search engines (Bing, Brave Search) rank within a domain.

### Why `lastmod` uses `handoffDate` for case studies

The `handoffDate` is the *meaningful* date for a case study — it's when the story is complete. Updating `lastmod` on every rebuild would force crawlers to re-fetch every case-study page on every deploy, wasting crawl budget. The handoff date stays stable until we genuinely add/edit a case study, at which point the JSON change re-deploys with a new `lastmod`.

For `/work` itself, `lastmod = max(handoffDate)` — when a new case study lands, the index's `lastmod` bumps and crawlers refresh the listing.

For static pages (`/`, `/services`, `/about`, `/get-in-touch`), `lastmod = BUILD_TIME`. Copy on these pages is more likely to evolve with the brand, so a build-aligned timestamp is the honest signal.

### Next.js `app/sitemap.ts` reference implementation

```ts
import type { MetadataRoute } from 'next';
import caseStudies from '@/content/case-studies.json';

const BASE = 'https://lastagency.com';

export default function sitemap(): MetadataRoute.Sitemap {
  const buildDate = new Date();

  const staticRoutes: MetadataRoute.Sitemap = [
    { url: `${BASE}/`,             lastModified: buildDate, changeFrequency: 'monthly', priority: 1.0 },
    { url: `${BASE}/services`,     lastModified: buildDate, changeFrequency: 'monthly', priority: 0.9 },
    { url: `${BASE}/about`,        lastModified: buildDate, changeFrequency: 'yearly',  priority: 0.7 },
    { url: `${BASE}/get-in-touch`, lastModified: buildDate, changeFrequency: 'yearly',  priority: 0.7 },
  ];

  const caseRoutes: MetadataRoute.Sitemap = caseStudies.map((cs) => ({
    url: `${BASE}/work/${cs.slug}`,
    lastModified: new Date(cs.handoffDate),
    changeFrequency: 'yearly',
    priority: 0.8,
  }));

  const latestHandoff = caseStudies
    .map((cs) => new Date(cs.handoffDate).getTime())
    .reduce((a, b) => Math.max(a, b), 0);

  const workIndex: MetadataRoute.Sitemap = [{
    url: `${BASE}/work`,
    lastModified: new Date(latestHandoff || buildDate.getTime()),
    changeFrequency: 'monthly',
    priority: 0.9,
  }];

  return [...staticRoutes, ...workIndex, ...caseRoutes];
}
```

---

## 3. Verification checklist for Architect

- [ ] `https://lastagency.com/robots.txt` returns the literal contents above (Next's `app/robots.ts` renders this).
- [ ] `https://lastagency.com/sitemap.xml` lists exactly 13 URLs: 5 static + `/work` index + 8 case studies — *no* `/thanks`, *no* `/404`.
- [ ] Each `/work/[slug]` entry's `lastmod` matches its `handoffDate` (ISO 8601, with timezone).
- [ ] Sitemap validates against `https://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9` schema.
- [ ] Run the sitemap through Google Search Console once production DNS is live (MANUAL-WORK item).
- [ ] When a case study is added/edited, the sitemap regenerates automatically at the next deploy — no manual sitemap edits.

---

## 4. Post-launch SEO ops (MANUAL-WORK references)

These are not Phase 2 deliverables but should land in `MANUAL-WORK.md`:

1. Submit `https://lastagency.com/sitemap.xml` to Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.
2. Verify domain ownership (DNS TXT record).
3. Set the preferred domain canonical to `https://lastagency.com` (no `www`).
4. Replace the Organization `sameAs` placeholders with real social URLs.
5. Add a 301 from `www.lastagency.com` → `lastagency.com` at the DNS/host layer.
